specification.problem: Classical quantum physical mapping (scheduling, placement, routing, ULB sizing) with a small testable circuit realization: a Clifford+T circuit mapped onto a line or grid of qubits via SWAP routing, verified by statevector equality up to qubit permutation.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: a 3-4 qubit Clifford+T circuit (e.g. H, T, CX gates) on a 2x2 or 1x4 grid. Build a QDFG, compute ASAP/ALAP slack, apply one pass of force-directed scheduling, place logical qubits on grid nodes, and route non-adjacent CX gates with SWAPs (3 CX each). Not covered: the ULB internals, FT code latencies, simulated-annealing placement iteration, congestion-aware routing, and the ULB size search except as a weighted-sum formula. The 40% latency result is not reproduced.

symbols.meaning: quantum dataflow graph; nodes are operations, edges are qubit values
earliest and latest level of operation v
distribution graph: expected number of type-k operations at level t
total force of placing v at level t
Manhattan distance between tiles of operations u and v
criticality weight of edge e, derived from slack
qubit permutation accumulated by SWAP routing
latency of FT operation o for ULB size b; frequency of o on critical paths

equations.label: Slack
equations.description: Time frame width of each operation in the QDFG; the candidate levels are ASAP..ALAP.
equations.abstract_quote: performs instruction scheduling based on a modified force-directed scheduling approach
equations.justification: Force-directed scheduling operates on time frames defined by ASAP/ALAP levels; the formula is standard, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Unit-latency levels, or latencies given as inputs

equations.label: Distribution graph and force
equations.description: Self force from the distribution graph plus predecessor and successor forces. Fix the (v,t) pair with the lowest force, then update time frames.
equations.justification: Classic force-directed scheduling (Paulin-Knight); the paper's modification is unknown.
assumptions: Delta p_v(t') is the change in v's occupancy probability at t'

equations.label: Timing-driven placement cost
equations.description: Placement minimizes the criticality-weighted Manhattan wirelength. The routing latency estimate is fed back to rescheduling.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions timing-driven placement and approximate routing latencies; the specific weight form is my choice.

equations.label: SWAP routing and correctness criterion
equations.description: Routing is implemented with SWAPs, and the mapped state must equal the original state up to the final permutation.
equations.justification: Circuit realization of routing chosen for testability; the abstract states no such relation.
assumptions: P_pi maps logical qubit i to its final physical position

equations.label: Weighted ULB size selection
equations.description: Pick the single ULB size minimizing the critical-path-frequency-weighted latency of FT operations.
equations.abstract_quote: using information about the occurrence frequency of operations on critical paths of the target quantum algorithm to weigh these latencies
equations.justification: The weighted-sum form is inferred from the described weighting of latencies by frequency.

registers.name: q
registers.size: n=3 or 4 (physical qubits on the grid, one per logical qubit)
registers.role: data qubits; the SWAP network permutes their contents; no ancillas

specification.initial_state: |0...0>, with the input circuit's Clifford+T gates applied to produce the reference state

steps.description: Build the QDFG from the small circuit, with serialization edges for multi-consumer values (no-cloning), and compute ASAP/ALAP levels and slack.
Run force-directed scheduling: compute forces, fix the lowest-force operation, update time frames, repeat.
Place logical qubits on grid nodes by minimizing the weighted Manhattan cost; add the routing latency estimate and reschedule until stable.
Route non-adjacent two-qubit gates by inserting SWAPs (3 CX each) along the shortest path, tracking the permutation; the actual latency is the schedule length plus the routing latency.
Compare the mapped and original statevectors after undoing the permutation; optionally compute the ULB size choice from given latencies.

specification.measurement: None; the statevector is read directly, with no measurements.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute total latency in cycles, undo the permutation on the mapped statevector, compute the fidelity, and evaluate the argmin over ULB sizes.
assumptions: The testable circuit is only a correctness check of a classical compiler
Tiny instance: 4 qubits on a 1x4 line with a few non-adjacent CX gates
Operation and ULB latencies are given inputs
No oracle or black box is used, so the query budget is zero
missing_information: Paper's exact force modification and QDFG construction
